items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
items.research_problem: LLMs face challenges of hallucination, outdated knowledge, and non-transparent reasoning processes that limit their reliability in knowledge-intensive tasks
items.methodology: Comprehensive survey and systematic literature review covering Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, and Modular RAG paradigms
key_findings: RAG paradigms evolved through three generations: Naive RAG (retrieve-then-generate), Advanced RAG (pre-retrieval, post-retrieval enhancements), and Modular RAG (flexible module composition)
The tripartite foundation of RAG includes retrieval, generation, and augmentation techniques
RAG effectively addresses hallucination by grounding generation in retrieved external knowledge
Evaluation frameworks and benchmarks are critical for advancing RAG systems
limitations: RAG systems face challenges in multi-hop reasoning and complex query understanding
Retrieval quality remains a bottleneck affecting overall system performance

items.title: Engineering the RAG Stack: A Comprehensive Review of the Architecture and Trust Frameworks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
items.research_problem: RAG research and engineering practices have become fragmented due to increasing diversity of methodologies, lacking a unified taxonomy and practical deployment framework
items.methodology: Systematic literature review spanning 2018-2025, covering academic studies, industrial applications, and real-world deployments
key_findings: RAG architectures encompass diverse fusion mechanisms, retrieval strategies, and orchestration approaches
A unified taxonomy consolidating existing RAG techniques is necessary for practical engineering
Trust and alignment frameworks are critical components for production RAG deployment
Quantitative assessment frameworks enable systematic evaluation of RAG system quality

items.title: Blended RAG: Improving RAG (Retriever-Augmented Generation) Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers
items.research_problem: RAG accuracy degrades as document corpora scale up, with retriever quality being the primary bottleneck
items.methodology: Empirical evaluation of blended retrieval methods combining Dense Vector indexes and Sparse Encoder indexes with hybrid query strategies
key_findings: Blending dense and sparse retrieval methods significantly improves RAG accuracy over single-method approaches
Hybrid query strategies outperform pure semantic or pure keyword search in retrieval quality
Blended RAG surpasses fine-tuning performance on generative Q&A datasets like SQUAD
The retriever component plays an outsized role in overall RAG system accuracy
